subject: Mass Media / Mass Communication (Code: 318)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Mass Media Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: When an individual engages in internal self-talk, personal reflection, meditation, or silent contemplation inside their own mind, this communication level is:
questions.explanation: Intrapersonal communication occurs entirely within the individual's mind, involving self-awareness, perception, thinking, and internal dialogue.

questions.question: A direct, two-way interpersonal communication exchange occurring specifically between two individuals (such as a doctor and a patient or two friends) is called:
questions.explanation: Dyadic communication refers to one-on-one interpersonal interaction between two people, allowing immediate reciprocal verbal and non-verbal feedback.

questions.question: In the study of non-verbal communication, the form of non-verbal interaction communicated through physical touch (such as a handshake, a comforting hug, or a tap on the shoulder) is:
questions.explanation: Haptics refers to communication through touch, which can convey intimacy, greeting rituals, reassurance, or dominance.

questions.question: The study of human body movement, gestures, facial expressions, and posture as a system of non-verbal communication is termed:
questions.explanation: Pioneered by Ray Birdwhistell, Kinesics is the study of how body movements, gestures, and facial expressions communicate non-verbal meaning.

questions.question: In Harold Lasswell's famous 1948 linear model of mass communication, which five core questions structure the communication process?
options: A) Who -> Says What -> In Which Channel -> To Whom -> With What Effect?
B) When -> Where -> Why -> How Much -> For How Long?
C) Speaker -> Speech -> Audience -> Occasion -> Applause?
D) Source -> Encoder -> Signal -> Decoder -> Destination?
questions.explanation: Lasswell's 5-element formula structures communication analysis: Who (communicator) says What (message) in Which Channel (medium) to Whom (receiver) With What Effect?

questions.sub_topic: Magic Bullet / Hypodermic Needle Theory Assumption
questions.question: What primary behavioral assumption did the early 'Hypodermic Needle' (Magic Bullet) theory make about media audiences in the 1920s and 1930s?
options: A) Audiences critically negotiate and reject dominant media messages through personal skepticism
B) Audiences are completely passive, uniform, and defenseless, directly and instantly absorbing media messages like a chemical injection with direct, predictable effects
C) Media messages have zero psychological influence on human beliefs or behavior
D) Audiences must possess a university degree before media messages can affect them
questions.explanation: The Hypodermic Needle model assumed that mass media messages are directly 'injected' into passive, atomized audiences, producing immediate, uniform behavioral responses.

questions.sub_topic: Antonio Gramsci: Common Sense vs Good Sense in Hegemony
questions.question: In Gramscian cultural theory, what is the crucial philosophical distinction between 'Common Sense' (senso comune) and 'Good Sense' (buon senso)?
options: A) 'Common sense' is learned exclusively in university classrooms, while 'good sense' is learned on television
B) 'Common sense' is written in legal statutes, while 'good sense' is printed on commercial advertising billboards

C) 'Common Sense' is the uncritical, fragmented everyday consensus that absorbs and naturalizes ruling-class hegemony, whereas 'Good Sense' is the rigorous, critical philosophical thinking that deconstructs hegemonic assumptions
D) There is no distinction; Gramsci used both terms as exact synonyms for traditional religious beliefs
questions.explanation: Gramsci distinguished uncritical common sense (incoherent everyday folklore naturalizing oppression) from good sense (coherent, critical consciousness needed for revolutionary emancipation).

questions.question: The visual title banner appearing at the very top of the front page of a newspaper that displays the publication's name (such as The Hindu or The Indian Express) is the:
questions.explanation: The masthead (or nameplate/flag) is the prominent designed title banner printed at the top of a newspaper's front page.

questions.question: The large-type line of text displayed prominently above a news article that summarizes the story's main point and attracts the reader's attention is the:
questions.explanation: A headline is the prominent heading at the top of an article that encapsulates the news angle in brief, compelling words.

questions.question: The opening sentence or paragraph of a news article that delivers the most essential facts of the story to the reader is termed the:
questions.explanation: The lead (traditionally spelled 'lede' to distinguish from lead metal type) is the introductory paragraph establishing the core news facts.

questions.question: A media event organized by a government official, public figure, or corporation to make a major public announcement and take questions from assembled journalists is a:
questions.explanation: A press conference is an organized gathering where a newsmaker delivers a statement and answers questions from reporters.

questions.question: Why did the 'Inverted Pyramid' format become the universal standard structure for hard news reporting in modern journalism?
options: A) It requires the story to end with an unexpected dramatic surprise twist to entertain readers
B) It saves printing press ink by forcing all sentences to be printed in triangular shapes
C) It ensures that all sources quoted in the article remain completely anonymous
D) It places the most critical 5Ws and H facts at the top, allowing hurried readers to grasp the core story instantly and enabling editors to trim from the bottom without losing vital facts
questions.explanation: The Inverted Pyramid arranges news by descending importance: essential facts first, background details later, facilitating quick reading and bottom-up trimming.

questions.question: What is the primary professional role of an 'Ombudsman' (or Readers' Editor) appointed within an independent newspaper organization?
options: A) An internal, independent official who investigates reader complaints about factual inaccuracies and ethical lapses, holding the newsroom accountable to public standards
B) To sell commercial advertising space to corporate retail department stores
C) To negotiate commercial labor contracts with mechanical printing press union workers
D) To deliver freshly printed newspaper bundles to suburban home delivery vendors
questions.explanation: An ombudsman acts as an internal reader advocate, examining errors, publishing corrections, and safeguarding journalistic integrity.

questions.sub_topic: Article 19(1)(a) Constitutional Synthesis: Free Speech and Press
questions.question: Although the Indian Constitution does not explicitly mention 'freedom of the press' in Part III, under which constitutional provision is press freedom recognized as an implicit fundamental right by the Supreme Court?
options: A) Article 14—the right to equality before the law and equal protection of the laws
B) Article 19(1)(a)—the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject only to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2)
C) Article 21A—the right to free and compulsory elementary education
D) Article 356—provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in states
questions.explanation: Since Romesh Thappar (1950), the Supreme Court has consistently held that freedom of the press is an intrinsic component of Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression).

questions.question: A massive outdoor advertising structure typically erected along major urban highways and busy road intersections to display commercial advertisements to passing drivers and pedestrians is a:
questions.explanation: Billboards (or hoardings in India) are large-format outdoor Out-of-Home (OOH) advertising structures targeting vehicular and pedestrian traffic.

questions.question: Small, inexpensive print advertisements grouped together under specific category headings (such as 'Real Estate', 'Matrimonial', or 'Jobs') in a newspaper are called:
questions.explanation: Classified ads are text-based, column-inch notices organized by category (employment, real estate, matrimonial), distinct from visual display ads.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations: Public Relations
questions.question: An official written statement dispatched to media outlets by an organization to provide factual information or announce newsworthy developments is a:
questions.explanation: A press release is a standard written communication issued to journalists to announce newsworthy events, appointments, or products.

questions.question: In advertising and marketing planning, the specific group of consumers identified as the intended recipients of an advertising campaign (based on age, income, or lifestyle) is the:
questions.explanation: The target audience is the designated demographic/psychographic segment most likely to purchase the product, for whom marketing messages are tailored.

questions.question: What distinguishes a 'Public Service Announcement' (PSA) from a conventional commercial advertisement?
options: A) It is legally required to feature popular Bollywood movie actors in every broadcast
B) It is broadcast exclusively on shortwave radio frequencies during midnight hours
C) It promotes public welfare, social health, safety, or community awareness (such as polio vaccination or road safety) without promoting a commercial product for financial profit
D) It charges viewers a direct admission fee before the television message can be viewed
questions.explanation: PSAs are non-commercial messages broadcast in the public interest to raise awareness, change harmful social habits, or promote health and safety.

questions.topic: Advertising and Public Relations: Public Relations
questions.question: In corporate public relations, what materials typically comprise a comprehensive 'Press Kit' (Media Kit) handed to journalists at an event?
options: A) A box of expensive electronic consumer goods given to reporters to influence favorable coverage
B) A confidential corporate tax audit ledger showing internal financial balance sheets
C) A printed legal contract demanding that journalists agree not to ask critical questions
D) A press release, company backgrounder fact sheet, executive biographies, high-resolution photographs, and relevant product specification sheets
questions.explanation: A press kit bundles vital background resources—press release, company fact sheets, executive bios, and photos—to assist journalists in reporting accurately.

questions.question: In television and film pre-production, a sequence of illustrated drawings or sketches depicting the planned camera shots, actor positions, and scene transitions is a:
questions.explanation: A storyboard is a visual blueprint that maps out camera angles, shot framing, and action sequentially before filming begins.

questions.question: A studio display device mounted directly in front of the camera lens that reflects scrolling script text on a two-way mirror for the news anchor to read while looking at the camera is a:
questions.explanation: A teleprompter displays scrolling text over a beam-splitter mirror, enabling presenters to read scripts while maintaining direct eye contact with the camera.

questions.question: In television camerawork, what is the mechanical distinction between a 'Pan' and a 'Tilt'?
options: A) A Pan moves vertically up or down, while a Tilt moves horizontally left or right
B) A Pan physically rolls the camera along tracks, while a Tilt raises the hydraulic pedestal
C) A Pan moves the camera horizontally left or right on a fixed pivot, while a Tilt moves the camera vertically up or down on a fixed pivot
D) A Pan zooms the optical lens, while a Tilt changes the shutter speed of the sensor
questions.explanation: Panning rotates the camera horizontally on a fixed axis (left/right); tilting pivots the camera vertically on a fixed axis (up/down).

questions.sub_topic: Barn Doors on Studio Lighting Fixtures
questions.question: The adjustable metal flaps mounted on the four sides of a studio lighting fixture to control and shape the direction and spread of light are called:
questions.explanation: Barn doors are four adjustable black metal leaves attached to lighting units to cut off and direct light spill away from unwanted areas of the set.

questions.question: What is the correct chronological sequence of the three universal phases of television and film production?
questions.explanation: The three fundamental stages are Pre-production (planning/scripting), Production (filming/recording), and Post-production (editing/finishing).

questions.question: In a live multi-camera television studio, what is the primary operational responsibility of the 'Floor Manager' (Floor Director)?
options: A) To physically operate the master video switcher panel inside the production control room
B) To act as the Director's representative on the studio floor, directing talent, coordinating stage movements, and relaying cues via hand signals while maintaining studio discipline
C) To write the daily television program reviews for morning digital newspapers
D) To repair electrical transformers in the municipal power substation outside the building
questions.explanation: The Floor Manager oversees studio floor action, cues talent, relays director instructions silently via hand gestures, and coordinates floor crew.

questions.question: In audio physics and sound recording, the frequency or pitch of a sound wave is measured in cycles per second, known as:
questions.explanation: Frequency (number of acoustic wave cycles per second) corresponds to perceived pitch and is measured in Hertz (Hz).

questions.question: A mesh screen placed between a radio broadcaster's mouth and the studio microphone to eliminate harsh, blast-like plosive sounds (such as 'P' and 'B') is a:
questions.explanation: A pop filter disperses fast-moving air blasts produced by plosive consonants ('p', 'b'), preventing them from hitting the mic capsule and creating bass thumps.

questions.question: In commercial FM radio broadcasting, the on-air presenter who hosts music shows, interacts with callers, reads station links, and entertains listeners is a:
questions.explanation: A Radio Jockey (RJ) is the on-air personality hosting radio programs, engaging listeners with lively talk, music curation, and interviews.

questions.question: In radio drama and film audio production, custom sound effects created by human Foley artists using everyday physical props (such as footsteps, rustling coats, or opening doors) are:
questions.explanation: Named after Jack Foley, Foley involves physically performing and recording everyday sound effects in synchronization with action to enrich dramatic reality.

questions.question: Why are 'Dynamic Microphones' (such as the Shure SM7B or SM58) widely preferred over delicate condenser microphones for field news reporting and noisy studio environments?
options: A) They record audio exclusively in 5.1 surround sound without using audio cables
B) They convert human speech directly into printed English text on computer screens
C) They are physically rugged, do not require external phantom power, handle high sound pressure levels without distortion, and are less sensitive to ambient background room noise
D) They require continuous refrigeration to keep their magnetic coils from melting
questions.explanation: Dynamic microphones operate on electromagnetic induction; their robust diaphragms handle rough field handling and high SPL without needing phantom power.

questions.sub_topic: Radio Club of Bombay (1923) First Broadcast
questions.question: In what historic year did the very first amateur radio broadcast in India take place, transmitted by the Radio Club of Bombay in June?
questions.explanation: Broadcasting in India began in June 1923 when the Radio Club of Bombay transmitted the first experimental amateur program, followed by the Calcutta Radio Club in November 1923.

questions.question: In a motion picture production crew, who is the creative and technical head responsible for camera operation, lighting design, shot composition, and visual photographic tone?
questions.explanation: The Director of Photography (DoP) collaborates with the director to establish the visual aesthetic, supervising camera operators and lighting crews.

questions.sub_topic: First Indian Feature Film: Raja Harishchandra (1913)
questions.question: Which historic silent motion picture, produced and directed by Dadasaheb Phalke in 1913, is recognized as India's first full-length indigenous feature film?
questions.explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke's 'Raja Harishchandra' (released May 3, 1913 at Coronation Cinema, Bombay) was India's first full-length silent feature film.

questions.question: Which influential film movement emerged in postwar Italy in the 1940s (exemplified by De Sica's 'Bicycle Thieves'), characterized by on-location shooting, non-professional actors, and gritty social realism?
questions.explanation: Italian Neorealism (Rossellini, De Sica, Visconti) brought gritty authenticity by shooting on bombed postwar streets with non-professional actors and everyday moral struggles.

questions.question: In cinematic visual grammar, what is the specific narrative function of an 'Establishing Shot' (usually an extreme long shot or wide shot)?
options: A) To display the closing copyright and distribution legal credits at the end of the film
B) To capture an actor's subtle teardrop in an extreme high-magnification close-up
C) To test whether the motion picture projector lamp is functioning properly
D) To establish the physical setting, location, time of day, and spatial relationship between characters at the beginning of a scene
questions.explanation: An establishing shot sets the scene context, orienting viewers to the physical geography, architecture, time, and scale before cutting to tighter drama.

questions.sub_topic: Satyajit Ray: Pather Panchali (1955) and Cannes Triumph
questions.question: Which internationally celebrated masterpiece, directed by Satyajit Ray in 1955 as the first installment of the Apu Trilogy, won the 'Best Human Document' award at the Cannes Film Festival?
questions.explanation: Satyajit Ray's lyrical debut 'Pather Panchali' (Song of the Little Road, 1955) put Indian cinema on the global map, winning Best Human Document at Cannes 1956.

questions.sub_topic: Hiralal Sen and F.B. Thanawala: Early Indian Film Pioneers
questions.question: Prior to Dadasaheb Phalke's full-length feature, which Calcutta photographer and filmmaker recorded stage plays and political swadeshi rallies on celluloid film starting in 1898?
questions.explanation: Hiralal Sen formed the Royal Bioscope Company in 1898 in Calcutta, filming scenes from popular Bengali plays, making him one of India's earliest documentary/short film pioneers.

questions.question: Any form of media content—such as blog posts, videos, comments, reviews, or digital images—created and uploaded by unpaid regular users of an online platform rather than professional media companies is:
questions.explanation: User-Generated Content (UGC) is published material created by regular consumers/users rather than traditional corporate media publishers.

questions.question: An online social media communication service (such as X, formerly Twitter) that allows users to broadcast short text messages, links, and media within strict character limits is a:
questions.explanation: Microblogging platforms enable users to share short, frequent digital status updates, links, and commentary (e.g., X, Threads, Mastodon).

questions.question: In digital social media culture, an individual who deliberately posts inflammatory, digressive, hostile, or offensive comments in online forums to provoke anger, derail discussion, and upset participants is a:
questions.explanation: An internet troll intentionally posts provocative, disruptive, or offensive remarks to incite emotional reactions and disrupt constructive conversation.

questions.question: Digital media content (such as a funny video or catchy meme) that achieves explosive, rapid popularity and widespread distribution across the internet via peer-to-peer social sharing is termed:
questions.explanation: Viral content spreads rapidly and organically across social networks through exponential word-of-mouth and user re-sharing.

questions.question: In digital consumer psychology, what does the pervasive phenomenon known as 'FOMO' (Fear of Missing Out) describe?
options: A) A physical medical phobia of looking at computer monitor displays in the dark
B) A legal regulation requiring individuals to delete old social media posts annually
C) A persistent social anxiety that others are having rewarding experiences from which one is absent, driving compulsive, habitual checking of social media feeds
D) A technical malfunction where mobile internet connections lose signal in elevators
questions.explanation: FOMO is social anxiety driven by viewing idealized peer updates, triggering compulsive checking behaviors and dependency on notification loops.

questions.sub_topic: Social Media Engagement Metrics (Likes, Shares, Comments)
questions.question: Why do social media recommendation algorithms weigh 'Shares' and 'Meaningful Comments' significantly higher than passive 'Likes' when ranking content in user feeds?
options: A) Because clicking a 'Like' button consumes three times as much computer battery electricity
B) Because comments can only be written by registered corporate commercial business accounts
C) Because social media platforms are legally required by international law to delete all likes
D) Because sharing and commenting require higher active user effort and cognitive investment, signaling deeper emotional resonance and stronger potential to spark viral discussions
questions.explanation: Active interactions (shares, long comments) reflect high user commitment and discussion value, signaling superior engagement quality to ranking algorithms.

questions.question: What is the standard markup language used to structure and format webpages, text documents, and multimedia elements across the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the fundamental standard markup language that structures webpages and applications on the World Wide Web.

questions.question: A digital audio program formatted as episodic audio files that users can download or stream on demand to personal devices (combining 'iPod' and 'Broadcast') is a:
questions.explanation: Coined by Ben Hammersley in 2004 (from 'iPod' and 'broadcast'), a podcast is an episodic series of digital audio files syndicated for on-demand playback.

questions.question: A fraudulent digital cyber attack where criminals send deceptive emails or messages pretending to be reputable banks or institutions to trick victims into revealing sensitive passwords or credit card numbers is:
questions.explanation: Phishing is social engineering deception where fraudulent messages impersonating trusted entities lure users into divulging credentials or financial data.

questions.question: What is the defining technological and philosophical difference between 'Web 1.0' (the 1990s web) and 'Web 2.0' (the participatory web)?
options: A) Web 1.0 operated without any electricity, while Web 2.0 operates entirely on solar battery power
B) Web 1.0 was written exclusively in ancient Greek, while Web 2.0 is written in English
C) Web 1.0 was used only inside military submarines, while Web 2.0 is used on airplanes
D) Web 1.0 was a read-only web of static, one-way informational webpages, whereas Web 2.0 is a read-write interactive web powered by user-generated content, collaboration, and social networks
questions.explanation: Tim O'Reilly coined Web 2.0 to signify the shift from static, read-only institutional websites (Web 1.0) to interactive, participatory, user-generated social ecosystems.

questions.question: In modern online journalism and digital information design, an 'Infographic' combines which elements to convey complex statistics clearly?
options: A) Visual graphic design, data charts, maps, and concise explanatory text to present complex data and patterns quickly and clearly to the reader
B) Long, uninterrupted blocks of sixty thousand words of plain black text without any illustrations
C) Audio recordings of classical violin music played over blank white computer screens
D) Commercial television advertisements featuring professional wrestling athletes
questions.explanation: An infographic synthesizes visual icons, data visualization (charts/graphs), and concise typography to communicate complex information rapidly.

questions.topic: New Media: Cyber Law and Governance
questions.sub_topic: IT Act, 2000 (India): Section 66A Supreme Court Invalidation (Shreya Singhal, 2015)
questions.question: In the landmark constitutional free speech judgment 'Shreya Singhal v. Union of India' (2015), the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 because:
options: A) The Information Technology Act had not been signed into law by the President of India

B) Its vague and overbroad terms (criminalizing online messages that cause 'annoyance' or 'inconvenience') lacked clear definitions, creating an unconstitutional chilling effect on free speech under Article 19(1)(a)
C) The statutory provision applied exclusively to messages sent via analog facsimile telegraph machines
D) Parliament is legally prohibited by the Constitution from passing any laws governing computer networks
questions.explanation: In Shreya Singhal (2015), the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A, holding that vague terms like 'annoyance' or 'offensive' criminalized legitimate speech without falling within Article 19(2) exceptions.
